chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Trimming the moustache and the nails from Friday to Friday is a safety from leprosy.

key_terms.أَخْذُ: Trimming or cutting (specifically of hair or nails)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical benefit of trimming the moustache and nails on Fridays according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the weekly grooming ritual of trimming the mustache and nails to protection from leprosy (al-judham), reflecting the Shia emphasis on physical purity (taharah) as a precursor to spiritual cleanliness. This practice is rooted in the Prophetic tradition of preparing for the Friday congregational prayer, where cleanliness is considered a manifestation of faith and a means of attracting divine mercy. The specific mention of leprosy highlights the belief in the tangible health benefits of regular hygiene within the broader framework of Islamic self-care.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said:
‘Trimming the moustache and the nails from the Friday to the Friday is a safety from the leprosy’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Trimming one’s mustache, and fingernails every Friday is protection against leprosy.’”
